presentation.question: Can the shared county shell carry one complete learning run?
presentation.opening: Nine frozen steps on the Clew Bay material: hear farraige, keep the coast's words distinct, build, type, use and speak the origin line, then gather what you can do and return to what slipped.
presentation.evidenceLimit: This is an internal fixture for the D29 freeze. It makes no historical claims and awards no county completion.
presentation.tegCanDo: Fixture capabilities only — not an awarded qualification.

targetWords.anchor: Clew Bay as a maritime world

chapters.title: An Bá · Clew Bay fixture run

pages.title: Tap what you hear
pages.body: The word belongs to the water you are looking at.

exercise.objective: Recognise farraige by sound as the sea that defines this coast.
exercise.prompt: Hear farraige and choose its meaning — you can answer whenever you are ready.
exercise.feedback: Farraige is the sea that makes this coast a working world.
exercise.hint: Listen for the rolling middle sound: far-ig-eh.

learningContract.objective: Recognise farraige by sound as the sea that defines this coast.

misconceptions.rationale: The learner names the land in the water rather than the water itself.
The learner reaches for a familiar coast word, caisleán, instead of the water word.
A response the named misconceptions do not cover.
misconceptions.feedback: Replay farraige and keep it on the open water.

learningContract.successFeedback: Farraige is the sea that makes this coast a working world.
learningContract.hint: Listen for the rolling middle sound: far-ig-eh.

recovery.guidance: That answer names something on the water rather than the water. Replay farraige and try again.
recovery.requiredResponse: Choose the meaning of farraige again after the replay.

pages.title: Tap the matching pairs
pages.body: Match each Irish word to what it names on this coast.

exercise.objective: Connect the opening headwords to their meanings.
exercise.prompt: Match each Irish word to its meaning.
exercise.feedback: Sea, bay and place — the coast now has three distinct names.
exercise.hint: Replay the words. Farraige is the open water; bá is the sheltered inlet; áit is the named coast.

learningContract.objective: Connect the opening headwords to their meanings.

misconceptions.rationale: Sea, bay and place blur into one undifferentiated coast word.
misconceptions.feedback: Those two do not belong together. Farraige is the open water; bá is the sheltered inlet; áit is the named coast.

learningContract.successFeedback: Sea, bay and place — the coast now has three distinct names.
learningContract.hint: Replay the words. Farraige is the open water; bá is the sheltered inlet; áit is the named coast.

recovery.guidance: Those two do not belong together. Keep the first word selected and try another meaning.
recovery.requiredResponse: Pair every Irish word with the meaning that belongs with it.

pages.title: Build the sentence
pages.context: Is as Maigh Eo mé · I am from Mayo
pages.body: Use the frame to place yourself on this coast.

exercise.objective: Produce a complete origin sentence with the as … mé frame.
exercise.feedback: Is as Maigh Eo mé — origin stated in one clean frame.
exercise.hint: The frame runs Is as [place] mé.

learningContract.objective: Produce a complete origin sentence with the as … mé frame.

misconceptions.rationale: The origin frame's word order slips when the pieces are separate tiles.

learningContract.successFeedback: Is as Maigh Eo mé — origin stated in one clean frame.
learningContract.hint: The frame runs Is as [place] mé.

recovery.requiredResponse: Build the line again from the tiles.

pages.title: Type the sentence
pages.context: Is as Maigh Eo mé · I am from Mayo
pages.body: The same line, now from your own keyboard.

exercise.objective: Produce the origin line unsupported — no tiles, no model replay.
exercise.feedback: Typed whole, without tiles — the frame is yours now.
exercise.hint: Keep the frame Is as [place] mé. The fada row gives you é.
exercise.recovery: The frame is close. Keep the order Is · as · Maigh Eo · mé, with the fada on mé.

learningContract.objective: Produce the origin line unsupported — no tiles, no model replay.

misconceptions.rationale: The fada on mé is dropped when the line is typed from memory.
misconceptions.feedback: Keep the fada on mé — the fada row gives you é.

misconceptions.rationale: The origin frame's word order slips without the tiles.
misconceptions.feedback: Keep the order Is · as · Maigh Eo · mé.

learningContract.successFeedback: Typed whole, without tiles — the frame is yours now.
learningContract.hint: Keep the frame Is as [place] mé. The fada row gives you é.

recovery.guidance: The frame is close. Keep the order Is · as · Maigh Eo · mé, with the fada on mé.

pages.title: Meeting on the shore
pages.body: A walker stops beside you on the shore path.

exercise.objective: Use the origin line inside a short present-day exchange.
exercise.prompt: A walker greets you on the shore above Clew Bay. Take your turns.
exercise.feedback: Three turns held — you placed yourself and closed the exchange.
exercise.hint: The origin frame Is as … mé answers where you are from.
exercise.recovery: That reply does not fit this turn. The conversation waits — choose another.

replies.diagnostic: That says goodbye, and the conversation has only begun. Answer the question instead.
That names the sea, not where you are from. Use the origin frame: Is as … mé.

replies.gloss: I am … — say your own name.

replies.diagnostic: That names the bay, not your name. Give your name, or ask back.

learningContract.objective: Use the origin line inside a short present-day exchange.

misconceptions.rationale: A reply that belongs to another turn is offered for this one.
misconceptions.feedback: That reply does not fit this turn. Answer the question the walker asked.

misconceptions.rationale: A coast word stands in where the exchange asks about the speaker.
misconceptions.feedback: That names a thing on the coast, not where you are from. Use the frame about yourself.

learningContract.successFeedback: Three turns held — you placed yourself and closed the exchange.
learningContract.hint: The origin frame Is as … mé answers where you are from.

recovery.guidance: That reply does not fit this turn. The conversation waits — choose another.
recovery.requiredResponse: Choose a fitting reply for the open turn.

pages.title: Choose what it means
pages.context: The bay · the words · the frame
pages.body: One short note on how the pieces sit together.

exercise.objective: Connect the Clew Bay words and the origin frame to what they say.
exercise.prompt: Read the note or hear the line, then choose what the line says.

options.rationale: The frame as … mé places the speaker; Maigh Eo is Mayo.

options.text: I am from the open sea.
options.rationale: Maigh Eo is Mayo, not the sea.

exercise.modelText: On this coast the open sea is farraige, the sheltered bay is bá, and a named place is áit. With the frame as … mé you can place yourself here.
exercise.feedback: The line places the speaker in Mayo — the coast's words and the origin frame agree.
exercise.hint: Read the frame as … mé literally: from Mayo am I.

learningContract.objective: Connect the Clew Bay words and the origin frame to what they say.

misconceptions.rationale: Farraige is bent into an origin it does not state.
misconceptions.feedback: That bends farraige into an origin; the line names a county, not the water.

misconceptions.rationale: Bá is kept while the origin frame the line is built on is dropped.
misconceptions.feedback: That keeps bá but drops the origin frame the line is built on.

misconceptions.rationale: A response the named misconceptions do not cover.
misconceptions.feedback: Read the frame as … mé literally: from Mayo am I.

learningContract.successFeedback: The line places the speaker in Mayo — the coast's words and the origin frame agree.
learningContract.hint: Read the frame as … mé literally: from Mayo am I.

recovery.guidance: That reading bends one of the coast's words out of shape. Keep Maigh Eo as Mayo.
recovery.requiredResponse: Read the note again and choose what the line says.

pages.body: The run's own record chooses the target.

exercise.objective: Re-enter one struggled target from its original sound or sentence — never a bare retype.
exercise.prompt: One target from this run, met again where it slipped.
exercise.feedback: The slipped target holds this time.
exercise.hint: Replay the original sound, then answer as you did before.
exercise.recovery: Close. Replay the sound and keep each word in its place.

exercise.objective: Hear farraige again and place its meaning.
exercise.prompt: Hear the word again, then choose its meaning.
exercise.feedback: Farraige holds as the sea this time.
exercise.recovery: Replay farraige once more and keep it on the open water.

exercise.objective: Restore the origin line from its original sound.
exercise.prompt: Hear or read the line, then type it whole.
exercise.feedback: The origin line holds whole this time.
exercise.hint: Is · as · Maigh Eo · mé, with the fada on mé.
exercise.recovery: Replay the line and restore each word in its place.
